summary: Summation No. 29 covers February 1948 (with most economic statistics for January or December). Politically it is dominated by the resignation of the Katayama Cabinet on 10 February after the Social Democratic left wing revolted over rail and postal rate rises in a supplementary budget, followed by a prolonged contest in which the Democratic leader Hitoshi Ashida was chosen prime minister over Liberal Shigeru Yoshida. The report also covers the hunt for hoarded goods, the National Diet Library Law, purge screening totals, police decentralization, war-crimes trials, and the prosecution's summation before the International Military Tribunal for the Far East. Economic sections give January output for coal, steel, textiles, power and transport, the 1947 foreign-trade totals, price controls, banking and liquidation figures, and reparations transfers. Social sections report nutrition surveys, the 1 October 1947 census (79.6 million), education conferences and media. Historians will find the Cabinet-crisis narrative and the quantitative series most useful.
highlights: The Katayama Cabinet resigned on 10 February, after eight months in office, when the Social Democratic left wing refused the supplementary budgets that raised railway and postal rates.

After weeks of interparty talks, Democratic leader Hitoshi Ashida was elected prime minister with 216 votes in the House of Representatives, though the Councillors favored Yoshida; the Lower House choice prevailed.
Hoarded and concealed goods worth about 1,400,000,000 yen were uncovered between November and January; a Diet committee probed members, and a comprehensive inventory of critical goods was ordered.
The National Diet Library Law passed both Houses unanimously on 4 February, creating a national library modeled on the Library of Congress after the 1947 United States Library Mission.

Purge screening provisionally designated 202,413 persons by 21 February, 173,602 of them finally; 163 of 1,424 information-media officials screened were barred, and the Hirano court injunction was ruled void.
At the Tokyo war crimes trial the defense ended surrebuttal on 10 February and the prosecution began its summation on 11 February against 25 defendants.
Japan's 1947 trade was about $526,000,000 in imports and $175,000,000 in exports, with roughly 92 percent of imports from the United States and foodstuffs 58 percent of import value.
The 1 October 1947 census counted 79,626,729 persons, about 5.6 percent above 1946; Bank of Japan notes outstanding stood at 215,219,000,000 yen on 29 February.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of Summation No. 29 (February 1948), table of contents for Parts I-IV, and lists of charts, maps and tables numbered 1-113.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no change in SCAP organization, Katayama's resignation and Ashida's election, January output figures, and social items including the 1 October 1947 census.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: States that the non-military organization of GHQ SCAP did not change during February 1948.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Katayama Cabinet resigned 10 February and Ashida was elected prime minister; also hoarded-goods drive, National Diet Library Law, 202,413 provisional purge designations, police decentralization and war-crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: January output in agriculture, mining, industry, textiles and transport, plus 1947 trade totals, finance, antitrust (267 concerns designated), reparations and science.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Nutrition surveys, venereal disease campaign, the 79,626,729 census total, education and Christian conferences, and a newspaper survey covering 2,978 papers.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed account of the Katayama Cabinet crisis and Ashida's election, hoarded goods, purge, police and crime statistics, and war-crimes trials including the IMTFE prosecution summation.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Katayama Cabinet fell 10 February over rate increases; Ashida elected prime minister with 216 votes; hoarded-goods inquiries, Diet Library Law, and purge screening of 671,120 persons.

sections.title: Cabinet Crisis
sections.summary: Social Democratic left wing opposed the rate-increase budget bills; the Cabinet decided 7 February to pass the issue to the Diet; Katayama resigned 10 February.

sections.title: Record of the Katayama Cabinet
sections.summary: Review of the cabinet's eight months: Ministry of Labor created, Home Ministry dissolved, eight-point economic program, anti-hoarding drive and the Law for Decentralization of Excessive Concentrations.

sections.title: Election of New Prime Minister
sections.summary: Interparty conferences from 10 February and Democratic and Social Democratic programs; Ashida elected in the Lower House, Yoshida in the Upper, ending in joint committee deadlock.

sections.title: Hoarded Goods
sections.summary: About 1.4 billion yen of hidden goods found November-January, Economic Stabilization Board finds worth 100,000,000 yen, weapons seized at Kawasaki, and Diet committee probes including the Hara and Kondo cases.

sections.title: Political Parties and the Diet
sections.summary: Party positions in the crisis, National Diet Library Law of 4 February, Central Liaison Office dissolved, Liberal wins in Upper House by-elections, and a 26 February fire at the purge records building.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: December crime and arrests, autonomous police in 1,604 of 1,808 municipalities, 82,760 prisoners in January, 943 railway accidents, and December fire losses.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Office of Attorney General began 15 February; Class B and C trial results; IMTFE defense surrebuttal ended 10 February and the prosecution's summation began 11 February.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and National War Crimes Trials
sections.summary: Attorney General's office, 85 investigations completed, 40 persons ordered apprehended, and 19 trials of 48 accused, including death sentences for Ishizaki and Katsudo.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: February IMTFE sessions, defense surrebuttal for Hirota and Taku, and the prosecution's summation on conspiracy, Manchuria, the Southwest Pacific and aggression against the USSR.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: January and February economic reporting on farm land sales, coal, metals, chemicals, manufacturing, textiles, transport, communications, labor, trade, prices, finance, property control and science.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Government sold 32,700 cho of land in January and purchased 94,655 cho on 2 February; also livestock population changes and fish landings.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Whaling catch of 271 blue whale units, January log production of 57,107,500 cubic feet, coal output of 2,829,200 tons, stockpiles of 667,200 tons, and crude oil production.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: January pig iron fell to 38,922 metric tons on hydroelectric shortage; coke stocks ended at 38,220 tons; cement 103,281 tons; ammonium sulfate 56,875 tons; machine tools 271 units; 17,084 coal-miner dwellings built since January 1947.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: January flour and food processing, pulp (down 2,230 tons), glass, optical and electrical goods, motor vehicles, leather (758,200 pounds), agricultural equipment and miscellaneous goods.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: January cotton yarn gained about 2,700,000 pounds on eased power limits; first postwar Egyptian cotton arrived (1,000 bales); raw silk fell to 6,209 bales; rayon staple dropped about 25 percent for lack of pulp.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 108,231 motor vehicles registered, 291,629,562 railway passengers, 1,480,747 tons of shipping cargo, electric generation of 2,233,000,000 kWh, and gas production.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Radiotelephone extended to Canada, Cuba and Mexico, radiotelegraph rates to the U.S. revised, and a December Ministry of Communications deficit of 1,208,818,199 yen.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Labor ministry ordinance of 7 February on illegal labor supply, anti-Communist union drives, no major strikes, union education programs, wages and employment security.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Calendar 1947 trade was about $526,000,000 imports and $175,000,000 exports, with 92 percent of imports from the United States.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Staple-food rations met in full, sugar incentive plan liberalized 19 February, price changes for explosives, rolling stock and cement, Tokyo water rates, and urban family expenditures.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 215,219,000,000 yen, Reconstruction Finance Bank loans, securities liquidation, tax receipts, supplementary budgets approved 24 February, and national debt.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: 943 looted ships recorded, 267 industrial firms designated excessive concentrations, antitrust orders, and 3,850 packages (7,294 tons) of advance reparations shipments.

sections.title: Section 13. Science and Technology
sections.summary: Science council's sixth meeting 30-31 January, 31 Japanese Standards promulgated, 103 patents granted, and Kyushu University research publications.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, nutrition, population, welfare, education, religion, cultural resources and information media for February 1948, including the 1947 census and textbook printing.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Nutrition surveys, venereal disease campaign, medical supply production, narcotics, public assistance, Red Cross, repatriation, and vital statistics including the 1947 census.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher conferences, authorization of 147,214,307 textbook copies, Christian conferences, first postwar art exchange, and press, radio and film reports.
